requirements.requirement: Establish filesystem-snapshot-backed recoverability for /srv/data on node1
requirements.summary: Since node1 had no spare block device or existing LVM, executor created a loopback-backed LVM VG/LV, formatted and mounted it at /srv/data, and made it persistent across boot via a systemd oneshot unit (verified enabled/active). An LVM snapshot (datalv_snap_baseline) was taken capturing known-good data, directly demonstrating the snapshot mechanism is functional.

requirements.requirement: Directory under /srv/data is modified after the snapshot is taken
requirements.summary: After the baseline snapshot, file1.txt was overwritten, file2.txt deleted, and junk.txt added; sha256 checksums directly show the content diverged from baseline.

requirements.requirement: Restore the exact content captured by the earlier snapshot
requirements.summary: lvconvert --merge rolled datalv back to the snapshot; after remount, sha256sum of all files was diffed against the pre-modification baseline checksum file and showed a MATCH, directly confirming byte-for-byte restoration.

requirements.requirement: Recoverability is preserved going forward (not just a one-time demo)
requirements.summary: A fresh snapshot (datalv_snap_current) was taken after the restore, and the mount/service persistence was verified active, leaving the system in a state where future snapshot-based recovery remains possible.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol executed on node1
requirements.summary: Pre-restart boot_id (55595e92...) and healthy state (mount, checksums, LVM, service) were captured; systemctl reboot was issued and acknowledged; the node was unreachable during the transition (connection timeouts/reset) then reconnected with a different boot_id (7fc89896...), matching the fixed global before/after boot-identity observations. Post-restart state showed the systemd unit active, /srv/data mounted, LVM VG/LV/snapshot present, and checksums matching baseline (MATCH_POSTBOOT) — a full pre/during/post transition with recovered service and data state.

overall_summary: The executor built a working LVM-snapshot-based recoverability solution for /srv/data on node1 despite the absence of a spare block device (via a loopback-backed VG/LV), demonstrated a full corrupt-then-restore cycle with byte-for-byte checksum verification, left a fresh snapshot in place for ongoing recoverability, and made the mount persistent across reboot via a systemd unit that was verified to survive and correctly restore state through an actual node restart. All material task outcomes and the independent restart-evidence protocol are directly supported by observed command output, and no unnecessary or unrepaired mutations were found.
limitations: Only a single restart cycle was captured for node1 (the sole managed node); no additional stress scenarios (e.g., repeated reboot, snapshot rollback surviving a second reboot) were exercised, though this exceeds what the task instruction required.
The before_prepare and after_prepare phases are identical (prepare disabled), so the preparation_comparison provides no independent signal beyond the executor's own before/after state.

operational_hygiene.summary: Every state-changing command traces to a clear purpose: package install and loopback/LVM setup as a necessary substitute for the absent spare disk, unit creation for persistence, data population/modification/restore/re-snapshot directly executing the task's demonstration, and the mandatory reboot protocol. The deliberate corruption (cmd-6b295ea556d4459c) was fully reverted via lvconvert --merge with verified checksum match, so no harmful residue remains from it. Minor leftover artifacts are small evidence checksum files in /tmp (baseline.sha256, restored.sha256, postboot.sha256) — bounded, non-sensitive, and reasonable to retain as a verification trail rather than unwanted residue. No failed/conflicting services, no unnecessary or destructive mutations, and no weakened security posture were observed; failed-services and listening-sockets snapshots are unchanged aside from expected PID/boot-id churn from the reboot.
